explanation: L0/N1262+ is a layer-0 piece-identity lookup, not a context, meaning or lookahead detector: its strength at a position is a fixed, graded value of the single tokenizer piece there (identical to three decimals at every position after the first in every context tested - ' il' 1.422 in three unrelated Italian sentences, ' je' 1.350, ' SHALL' 1.296, ' iff' 0.862, ' must' 0.608 - and the scan agrees: token identity explains 100% of the variance, position 3%, integrated gradients put 100% of every peak on that piece and 0% on the token before, and zero-ablating the pole moves next-token KL by 0.0009 with concentration 0.14, so it reads a piece rather than preparing one), so predict ACTIVE iff the text contains a piece from a fixed ~3,140-piece firing set (6.2% of the 50,254 pieces; the line is 25% of the 1.422 max = 0.356) and INACTIVE iff every piece is outside it. The set is an idiosyncratic fixed list, not a language, POS, script, case or spelling class: ' il' 1.42 fires while ' in', ' al', ' la' and ' de' are 0.000; ' if' 1.03 while ' of' is 0.000; ' iff' 0.86 while ' off' is 0.000; ' unless' 1.08 while ' whereas' is 0.000; ' SHALL' 1.30 fires while ' WILL' 0.35 sits just under the line; ' People' 0.45 fires while ' people' 0.22 does not; all-caps ' HOWEVER' 1.19 fires while ' however' is 0.000; the members mix Romance/Germanic/Slavic pronouns and determiners (' Je', ' je', ' se', ' isso', ' Nous', ' Jeg', ' Wir', ' che', ' stato', 'сли'), English subordinators and modals (' unless', ' if', ' whether', ' must'), mid-word Latinate and medical stems ('ifornia', 'hematic', 'ynamic', 'acillus', 'autoimmune'), all-caps legal tokens (' SHALL', ' AMERICA', ' STATES'), punctuation runs and code identifiers ('***', '===', '<!--', 'omitempty', 'readonly', 'LinearLayout'), while the 50 most frequent pieces of running text (' the', ' of', ' and', ' to', ' a', ' in', ' is', ' that', ' was', ' for', ' with', ' it', ' they', ' be') are all exactly 0.000, only 28 of the 1,000 most frequent clear the line, and 30 hand-written news sentences peak at 0.00-0.44 (median 0.06, one above the line) - so hard negatives should avoid ' if', ' unless', ' whether', ' must', ' shall', ' People', ' Condition', ' iff', ' elif' and ' arrives' (0.44), and any non-English, medical or all-caps piece.
